questions.enonce_markdown:
**SECTION A - DIRECTED WRITING (30 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content (14 marks); Expression and Accuracy (12 marks); Slanting (4 marks).

You are the president of your students' union. You came across this information on second hand clothes and you found it useful. Select relevant information from it and write an article for your magazine on the disadvantages of using second hand clothes and possible measures to prevent contamination if they must be used. Write in TWO paragraphs of not more than **150 words**. Your pen name is A.A.Flavour. Pay attention to grammar, punctuation, spelling and handwriting.

The sale of secondhand clothes is booming in the country, in different forms. In the past, secondhand clothes were synonymous to poverty. The rich and middle class bought their clothes from boutiques, but today it is no longer the case. The rich, the middle class, and the low income earners have practically adjusted their budgets and are now visiting these markets. Given that people of all economic levels are customers of this market, there is no social stigma attached to it. Shopping for secondhand clothing will give you the advantage finding clothes that no one else has. You will be unique without putting much effort into it and in addition, your purse will not feel a difference. Some people simply say such shopping is a great way to look good without having to spend a fortune.

Despite the demand and stampede surrounding the business, health experts have warned of the dangers of buying secondhand clothes. Many human diseases, especially sexually transmitted ones, are transmitted through body fluids such as blood, sweat, urine, semen, and so on. The causative organs implicated in a lot of these diseases have been isolated in clothes of people with these diseases. Infections such as skin candidiasis, scabies, ringworm, body lice, and chicken pox can be transmitted through clothes previously used by infected persons. The risk is even more if the clothes are not properly washed, disinfected and ironed before use. The category of clothing that is even more culpable is underwear which many people do not iron before use due to the material with which it is made, which does not allow it to withstand much heat.

If you happen to buy secondhand clothes, ensure that you use antiseptics to disinfect them, line them out in the sun, and iron them before use. For clothing that cannot be ironed directly such as underwear, you can do "shadow-ironing" by placing some material on it while it is still wet and then iron it till it gets dry. Another common practice is trying on clothes that you want to buy, to see if they fit. Desist from this practice; but if you must, always try them on without taking off your clothes. By this, you prevent them from getting in contact with your skin before you disinfect and iron them. Also, a careful examination of every item before you purchase it will give you an indication of its general cleanliness and quality, even though it will not necessarily reveal the health risk.

Items that are grossly soiled or contaminated should be discarded. Better still, avoid buying such clothing entirely. While few know the dangers that accompany secondhand clothes but decide to overlook them, many are in total darkness. Nonetheless, medical studies have shown many risks these common habits might pose. Although we may not notice them almost immediately we are infected, and even when we do so, we tend to deceive ourselves by admitting that we got the infections from elsewhere. In all, secondhand articles have become a rampant phenomenon where no one can cast a stone for never having used any secondhand product before. If not clothes, it would be electronics, footwear, home utensils, gadgets, or even automobiles. Yes, the list is endless.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (two paragraphs, 145 words, excluding the pen name)**

Fellow students, buying second hand clothes may look cheap, but it can seriously damage our health. Health experts warn that many diseases, especially sexually transmitted ones, pass through body fluids such as blood and sweat left in clothes. Skin candidiasis, scabies, ringworm, body lice and chicken pox can also spread through clothes worn earlier by infected people. The danger is greater when the clothes are badly washed, and underwear is the worst case because it cannot withstand much heat.

However, if you must buy such clothes, protect yourself. Disinfect them with antiseptics, dry them in the sun and iron them before use. Shadow-iron underwear by covering it with a damp cloth and ironing until it dries. Never try clothes on directly against your skin, and examine every item carefully before paying. Finally, discard anything soiled or contaminated. Your health is worth more than a bargain.

A.A.Flavour

**Why this works (selection and slanting).** The article has two jobs: to show the DISADVANTAGES of using second hand clothes and to give MEASURES to prevent contamination. Paragraph 1 therefore keeps only the health dangers (diseases carried by body fluids, the infections that spread through clothes, the extra risk of badly washed clothes and of underwear). Paragraph 2 keeps only the protective measures (antiseptics, sun, ironing, shadow-ironing, careful trying on, examining items, discarding soiled ones). The model drops every point that praises second hand clothes (they are cheap, no social stigma, you look unique, you spend little) and the points that are only comments (the market is booming, nobody can cast a stone, the list is endless). The words are the candidate's own, the tone suits a students' magazine (it speaks to "fellow students"), and the pen name A.A.Flavour is used as the signature instead of the candidate's real name.

**Marking guide**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content | 14 | Relevant points on BOTH parts of the task: the disadvantages (diseases, infections, risk of unwashed clothes and underwear) and the measures (disinfect, sun, iron, shadow-ironing, try on safely, examine, discard); no irrelevant points |
| Expression and Accuracy | 12 | Own words (no lifting of whole sentences), clear linking, correct grammar, spelling and punctuation, TWO paragraphs, 150 words at most |
| Slanting | 4 | Every point is turned against the use of second hand clothes or towards preventing contamination; the praise of cheap fashion in the passage is left out; the pen name A.A.Flavour is used |

**Common mistakes**

1. Copying sentences from the passage word for word: the instructions say indiscriminate copying earns no marks.
2. Using the advantages of second hand clothes (cheap, unique, no stigma), or giving only the disadvantages and forgetting the measures (or the reverse), so the answer is not slanted to the task.
3. Writing one paragraph or three, signing with the real name instead of A.A.Flavour, or going over 150 words.
